items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Bunny Briggs was with us for a long time, stumping for some of the acts.

ctx.x: Sidney's timing was impeccable, his execution in taste predominated, and he had excellent training, basically, I'm sure, but we never discussed it. He played a swinging, awe inspiring show. He loved to play behind great tap dancers, lines of girls dancing -- and shows in general. He enjoyed playing them, as much as he did jazz runs. And some of that rubbed off on me, thank goodness, because with Barnett's band, I had to play many, many shows; theatres. The Apollo Theatre, Washington's Howard Theatre -- these are…

And all the greatest at that time, and we had the original Cotton Club boys and girls -- wonderful dancers, and we had comedians, Pigmeat Markum and Avis and Estraledis, stepbrothers, and to me the greatest of all dancers was Baby Lawrence, the greatest jazz dancer. I don't think anybody could disprove that. And Bunny Briggs, too -- Bunny Briggs was with us for a long time, stumping for some of the acts. There were some of the acts, among many.
